newsitem.title: USA: First Midwest sees two special items in Q3. [CORRECTED 16:15 GMT]
newsitem.headline: First Midwest sees two special items in Q3. [CORRECTED 16:15 GMT]

text.p: First Midwest Bancorp Inc said Friday the net effect of two special items will be a positive effect on third-quarter earnings. One item is a gain and another a charge that will result in lower insurance premiums.
(Corrects to show one item a gain, one a charge.)
The items arise from federal legislation relating to the repeal of the thrift bad debt recapture regulations and the recapitalization of the Savings Association Insurance Fund.
It said a $992,000 bad debt recapture expense taken in the 1995 fourth quarter will be reversed and recorded as third quarter income.
First Midwest also said based on SAIF-insured deposits acquired over the years, the company will incur a one-time after-tax charge in the quarter of $962,000.

As a result of this one-time special assessment and based on SAIF-announced projections, First Midwest anticipates a reduction in ongoing deposit insurance premiums of approximately $300,000 annually.
First Midwest, a bank holding company, expects to release its earnings for the quarter on October 15.
